FORENSIC TESTING BACKLOGS

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Forensic Testing Serivce with the South African Police Serivce have grinded to a halt - we ask why and who should be held accountable.

Summary:
DNA Analysis is the greatest weapon we have against violent crimes ranging from GBV to rape, murder and armed robberies.

While we have access to the technology, the expertise and the experience. South Africa is facing a human rights crisis with unprecedented backlogs of forensic exhibits that have not been processed.

Further information:
There has been a 300% increase in the backlog of cases, +/- 90% of which are sexual assault cases. In November 2020 there was a backlog of close to 117736 cases just in the Western Cape, Eastern Cape, KZN and at the SAPS Headquarters. It is estimated to just over 90% of all outstanding analysis are sexual assault kits.

In March it was revealed in Parliament that figure has increased to 172000 cases. Not a single sample was processed in all of January and February this year. NOT ONE.
Former deputy chair of the National Forensic Oversight and Ethics Board, Vanessa Lynch and director of the DNA Project is outraged. This is a travesty of justice. South Africa is seen as the Jewel in the Crown of DNA analysis on the African Continent – but the country is quickly losing that status despite the infrastructure and skills
In 2020 concerns were raised about contract management, especially in light of the admission of lax contract management systems within the division.

The Forensic Sciences Laboratory said it need funds – treasury allocated an additional R250 million to the division’s operational baseline budget in November 2020 hoping it would improve functionality.

Fast forward 3 months and only 30% of this budget has been spent. Of the 5 contracts that have been waiting to be finalized for the last two years – only two have been finalized – three are still in limbo. The Head of SAPS forensic science labs Maj-Gen Edward Ngokha said his department faced insufficient funding and experienced instability at management level this week when the new appointed Forensic Oversight and Ethics Board appeared before the portfolio committee on Police this week.

HOW DO WE TELL THE STORY
PAINT A PICTURE OF WHAT DNA ANALYSIS CAN DO

Sikhangele Mki was arrested for general assault. His DNA-sample was run against the DNA Porject database. He was linked to multiple violent crimes.
He was convicted on 30 counts of rape, 20 counts of kidnapping, four counts of assault with intent to do grievous bodily harm, 12 counts of robbery with aggravating circumstances, six counts of attempted robbery with aggravating circumstances, two counts of robbery and three counts of attempted robbery.

He was convicted in the Western Cape High Court in 2017 and is now serving 15 life terms and 120 years imprisonment.

He was only caught and convicted after his DNA sample was run through South Africa’s DNA system.

THIS ISN’T HAPPENING. VIOLENT CRIMINALS ROAM FREE EVERY DAY PERPATRATING THESE CRIMES WITH IMPUNITY, BECAUSE EVEN IF THEY ARE CAUGHT THEY ARE NOT GOING TO BE CONVICTED ANY TIME SOON.

Ironically South Africa was recognized internationally for this case – as a global success case.

WHAT DOES THIS FAILURE OF JUSTICE DO TO VICTIMS OF VIOLENT CRIMES
Bring in MBali – we paint her not as a victim – but as a survivor. She lives has survived a sexual assault, but lives the secondary trauma every day because the DNA in her case from 14 months ago is not being processed.

What she wants is what government has enacted but not enforced. DNA samples should be processed within 30 days, Lynch explains “there is no question that DNA profiling is one of the most successful prosecutorial tools to identify rapists and violent criminals, due to its high rate of reliability in securing conviction. In short, justice delayed is justice denied”.

WHO NEEDS TO ANSWER

SAPS & THE ETHICS BOARD
1. SAPS allowed this situation to progress to this stage
2. The board does not have an enforceable plan of action. No one is being held liable

If we do not hold the authorities accountable how can we hold criminals accountable. Their inaction is criminal.

INTERVIEWS
1. Vanessa Lynch – DNA PROJECT – the value of DNA and the current status quo
2. Mbali – survivor or rape
3. SAPS – Head of Forensic Services Laboratories or maybe Brigadier Vish Naidoo
4. Insider – frustrated with processes – criminals caught but not brought to book
5. National Forensic Oversight & Ethics Board

STRUCTURE

VO: MURDER. ASSAULT. HIJACKING. ARMED ROBBERY. RAPE. VIOLENT CONTACT CRIMES ARE A DAILY REALITY FOR SOUTH AFRICANS.

LINK: THE BIGGEST WEAPON IN BRINGING THOSE OFTEN RUTHLESS CRIMINALS TO BOOK IS SCIENCE – DNA AND FORENSIC ANALYSIS CAN TIE CRIMINALS TO CRIME SCENES AND LINK THEM TO OTHER CASES.

VO: THE POWER OF DNA EVIDENCE HAS REVOLUTIONISED CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS

IN THE WESTERN CAPE, A MAN WAS ARRESTED FOR GENERAL ASSAULT. BUT THAT WAS NOT HIS ONLY CRIME. WHEN HIS DNA WAS PUT THROUGH THE DNA PROJECT DATABASE - THE RESULTS LINKED HIM TO MULTIPLE OTHER VIOLENT CRIMES.

IN THE END, SIKHANGELE MKI WAS CONVICTED OF 84 CHARGES WHICH INCLUDED FOUR COUNTS OF ASSAULT WITH INTENT TO DO GRIEVOUS BODILY HARM, 12 COUNTS OF ROBBERY WITH AGGRAVATING CIRCUMSTANCES, 27 COUNTS OF KIDNAPPING AND 30 COUNTS OF RAPE.

MKI IS NOW SERVING 15 LIFE TERMS AND 120 YEARS IMPRISONMENT. ALL BECAUSE OF THE DNA EVIDENCE THAT LINKED HIM TO THOSE VIOLENT CRIMES.

BUT TODAY, CASE VICTORIES LIKE THAT ARE FEW AND FAR BETWEEN.

LINK: NOT A SINGLE SAMPLE WAS FINALISED IN ALL OF JANUARY AND FEBRUARY THIS YEAR. NOT ONE.

VO: IN NOVEMBER 2020 THE NATIONAL FORENSIC SCIENCE LABORATORY HAD A BACKLOG OF 117 000 DNA AND FORENSIC EXHIBITS. BY THE BEGINNING OF MARCH THIS YEAR, THAT FIGURE CLIMBED TO AN UNPRECEDENTED 172787 CASES.

FORENSIC DNA CONSULTANT, VANESSA LYNCH, BELIEVES THIS IS A HUMAN RIGHTS CRISIS.

VANESSA: IT HAS REACHED CATASTROPHIC PROPORTIONS. //. M11 ULTIMATELY, THE GOVERNMENT IS FAILING THE VICTIMS BY ALLOWING // THE BACKLOG TO GET TO THIS PARTICULAR NUMBER, DELAYED JUSTICE IS ACTUALLY DENIED JUSTICE TO THE VICTIMS.

VO: AND THAT’S NOT AN EXAGGERATION ACCORDING TO A POLICE DETECTIVE WHO SPOKE TO US ON CONDITION OF ANONYMITY.

INSIDER: // SOME OF THESE CASES IS THROWN OUT OF COURT BECAUSE THE DNA ANALYSIS ISN’T FINISHED, THE RESULTS AREN’T THERE. M1 THE NPA IS VERY CLEAR, THE CASE MUST BE READY FOR TRIAL WITHIN SIX MONTHS OF THE PREPARATOR APPEARING IN COURT M15

VO: VIOLENT CRIMINALS ROAM FREE EVERY DAY PERPETRATING CRIMES WITH IMPUNITY, BECAUSE EVEN IF THEY ARE CAUGHT, THEY ARE NOT GOING TO BE CONVICTED ANY TIME SOON, EXPLAINS THE DETECTIVE.

INSIDER: WE DESPERATELY NEED THIS DNA TO PROVE, TO TRACE THE PERPETRATOR FIRST OF ALL AND TO PROVE THEIR PRESENCE ON THE CRIME SCENE. // CRIME WILL NEVER COME DOWN IF WE CAN’T KEEP THESE PEOPLE BEHIND BARS.

VO: MARK ROGERS REPRESENTS THE DNA BOARD THAT PLAYS AN OVERSIGHT ROLE, PROVIDING FEEDBACK TO THE PARLIAMENTARY PORTFOLIO COMMITTEE ON POLICE, IN TERMS OF ANY SHORTCOMINGS AND POSSIBLE SOLUTIONS WITHIN THE FORENSIC SCIENCES FRAMEWORK.

THE BOARD IS DEEPLY CONCERNED ABOUT THE CURRENT BACKLOGS.

MARK: // FOR EVERY SAMPLE THAT IS NOT ANALYZED AND NOT PROCESSED, IT REPRESENTS A PERPETRATOR THAT COULD POTENTIALLY BE A REPEAT OFFENDER// M11
DEREK: SO WHAT IS THE BOARD IDENTIFIED AS THE KEY ISSUES DRIVING THIS GROWING BACKLOG?
MARK: , THE PROBLEMS IN THE LABORATORY AND IN THE DIVISION OF FORENSIC SCIENCE AT THE MOMENT ARE ROOTED IN SYSTEMIC CHALLENGES WITHIN THE PROCUREMENT AND THE SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT ENVIRONMENT. M5

VO: MAJOR-GENERAL EDWARD NGOKHA HEADS UP THE POLICE FORENSIC SCIENCE LAB.

GENERAL: WE GOT TO THE SITUATION BECAUSE WE COULDN'T PROCESS ENOUGH WE DIDN'T HAVE ENOUGH CONSUMABLES TO DO THE PROCESSING.
DEREK: : BUT WHOSE FAULT WAS THAT?
GENERAL: CONSUMABLES HAS TO BE PROCUREMENT IN SOME WHERE IN THE SAPS SOMETHING WENT WRONG //THE LAB WAS READY TO BE FUNCTIONAL, BUT CAN ONLY FUNCTION IF THIS CONSUMABLES.M35

VO: GENERAL NGOKHA POINTS OUT THAT THE MAJORITY OF THE BACKLOG IS REFERENCE SAMPLES THAT WILL BE ADDED TO THE DNA DATABASE - HE SAYS ONLY 48% OF THE ENTIRE BACKLOG IS CRIME SAMPLES.

MBALI SHONGWE IS A SURVIVOR OF SEXUAL ASSAULT.

MBALI: IT'S BEEN SO DESENSITIZED AND IT'S BEEN SO NORMALIZED THAT I DON'T EVEN THINK THAT PEOPLE REALIZE THAT THERE IS A PERSON BEHIND THAT CASE OR THERE'S A PERSON BEHIND THAT SAMPLE//M8

VO: SIXTEEN MONTHS AFTER HER ATTACK, THERE HAS BEEN NO REAL PROGRESS ON THE CASE.

MBALI: TO HAVE MY CASE GO LIKE STAGNANT AND HAVE A STAND STILL JUST IS ANOTHER. IT'S A FURTHER PUSH DOWN AND IT JUST FEELS AS THOUGH THERE IS NO SUPPORT AND THERE IS NO CARE ABOUT WHAT HAPPENS.M4

VO: WHILE IT TAKES COURAGE TO REPORT A SEXUAL ASSAULT AND TO SUBMIT A RAPE KIT, IT OFTEN FEELS LIKE SECONDARY TRAUMA EXPLAINS MBALI, AS SHE REFLECTS ON THE PROCESS.

MBALI: IT'S SO INVASIVE. AND FOR YOU TO GO THROUGH THAT PROCESS AND TO HAVE IT STUCK IN A PILE LEFT. IT REINFORCE HOW THAT ATTACK WAS SUPPOSED TO MAKE YOU FEEL LIKE YOU DON'T MATTER, LIKE THIS IS NOT IMPORTANT. AND THESE ARE THE PEOPLE THAT YOU TURN TO FOR HELP. M8

VO: BUT THE COPS ON THE GROUND, INVESTIGATING THESE TYPES OF CASES, FEEL THEIR HANDS ARE TIED.

INSIDER: THE FAMILIES ACCUSE THE DETECTIVES DRAGGING THEIR FEET. BECAUSE YOU HAVE TO GIVE THEM THE SAME EXCUSES OVER AND OVER. AND IT'S STRESSFUL.

DEREK: WE ARE TOLD THAT NOT A SINGLE SAMPLE WAS PROCESSED DURING THE FIRST TWO MONTHS OF THE YEAR //
GENERAL: DURING THE MONTH OF JANUARY AND FEBRUARY, EVIDENCE RECOVERY WAS CARRYING ON, DNA EXTRACTION WAS CARRY ON. QUANTIFICATION COULDN'T CARRY ON // ONLY THE INITIAL PART WAS TAKING PLACE //. SO TO SAY THAT EVERYTHING WAS DEAD, IT IS INCORRECT. M10

VO: BUT THE LONG AND SHORT OF IT IS THAT THE SAMPLE ANALYSIS IS NOT BEING FINALISED, THESE CASES ARE NOT GOING TO COURT, REPEAT OFFENDERS ARE NOT BEING LINKED TO MULTIPLE CRIMES AND THE VICTIMS HAVE YET TO SEE JUSTICE.

DEREK: YOU CAN’T BE HAPPY….?!?
GENERAL: // I'M VERY CATEGORICAL ABOUT THAT I CAN’T BE HAPPY.

LINK: HAVING ACCESS TO THE TECHNOLOGY, THE EXPERTISE AND THE EXPERIENCE, WITHOUT CONSUMABLES, CHEMICALS AND MAINTAINED EQUIPMENT RENDERS SOUTH AFRICA’S FORENSIC LABS INEFFECTIVE

VO: IN AN ATTEMPT TO ADDRESS THE BACKLOG AND IMPROVE FUNCTIONALITY, TREASURY ALLOCATED AN ADDITIONAL R250 MILLION TO THE DIVISION’S OPERATIONAL BASELINE BUDGET IN NOVEMBER.

BUT FAST FORWARD 3 MONTHS AND ONLY 30% OF THIS BUDGET HAS BEEN SPENT AND THE BACKLOG HAS JUMPED BY MORE THAN 50 000 CASES.

DEREK: // WHY IS IT TAKING SO LONG?
GENERAL: YOU'LL REALIZE THAT THAT'S WHEN YOU USE THE MONEY TO BUY IN THROUGH QUOTATIONS. YOU CANNOT USE MUCH OF THAT FOR YOU TO BE ABLE TO BUY IN BULK IN NATURE OF YOUR CONTRACT M15

MARK: //CONTRACTS HAVE BEEN DELAYED FOR UNREASONABLE PERIODS OF TIME. //. // IF ONE CONTRACT IN THAT VALUE CHAIN HAS NOT BEEN AWARDED, IT HOLDS UP THAT ENTIRE PROCESS. M7
DEREK: IS IT CORRUPTION OR INEPTITUDE?
MARK: I THINK IT'S MORE JUST INEPTITUDE. IT'S PROBABLY JUST INEFFICIENCIES IN THE DEMAND PLANNING AND THE PROCUREMENT SYSTEMS AND PROCESSES. M7

LINK: THERE SEEMS TO BE A SCRAMBLE TO SET IN PLACE TURN AROUND PLANS AND IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES. YET, IT SEEMS NO ONE IS BEING HELD ACCOUNTABLE FOR THE INACTION THAT ALLOWED THIS MASSIVE BACKLOG TO ACCUMULATE.

VANESSA: WE TALK ABOUT CRIMINALS BEING ACCOUNTABLE, BUT IN FACT, THE GOVERNMENT HAS TO BE ACCOUNTABLE BECAUSE THEY ARE AS GUILTY AS THE CRIMINALS IF THEY'RE NOT FOLLOWING THROUGH ON THEIR PROMISES. M7

GENERAL: I CAN ONLY TALK ON BEHALF OF THE COMPONENT THAT I AM LEADING, WHICH IS SITTING WITH THE PROBLEM OF PROCESSING OF EXHIBITS. I DIDN'T HAVE THE CONSUMABLES TO DO THE PROCESSING AND I CAN NOT TAKE ACCOUNTABILITY. UNLESS IF I HAD CONSUMABLES// M35

VO: ROGERS EXPLAINS THE POLICE’S SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT STRUCTURES ARE AT THE CENTRE OF THE BACKLOGS.

MARK: THERE ARE CHALLENGES, LEADERSHIP CHALLENGES WITHIN THE SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT, ENVIRONMENT LEADERS WHO DID NOT ACT THE WAY THEY SHOULD HAVE ACTED. // I THINK CERTAINLY ACTION SHOULD BE TAKEN AGAINST THOSE RESPONSIBLE. M12

VO: WHILE THE NECESSARY CONTRACTS ARE NOW BEING PRIORITISED, OVERTIME BUDGETS HAVE BEEN APPROVED AND THERE ARE STRICT PROCESSES IN PLACE TO MONITOR PROGRESS, THE BACKLOG WILL NOT BE RECTIFIED INSTANTLY.

DEREK: ARE YOU TALKING ABOUT WEEKS OR MONTHS BEFORE WE START GETTING INTO THIS BACKLOG?
GENERAL: IN TERMS OF SCIENCE, IF YOU GET A BATCH OF CONSUMABLES TO TO USE IN A SYSTEM, YOU CANNOT JUST USE IT, YOU HAVE TO VALIDATE IT FIRST. SO WE NEED A BIT OF TIME TO VALIDATE, TO TAKE MAYBE A MATTER OF A MONTH OR TWO. M19

VO: SURVIVORS LIKE MBALI, ARE NOT OPTIMISTIC - THIS CRISIS HAS BEEN LOOMING FOR SOME TIME.

MBALI: I WILL ALWAYS HAVE SLEEPLESS NIGHTS WONDERING, IS THIS HAPPENING TO SOMEBODY ELSE? // WONDERING, LIKE, WHERE IS THIS PERSON AND WHY WAS NOTHING DONE ABOUT IT? AND I THINK THAT FOR ME, I'LL FEEL THAT WAY UNTIL I KNOW THAT JUSTICE HAS BEEN SERVED. M11

VO: BUT EVEN THE COPS INVESTIGATING THESE CASES ARE LOSING ALL HOPE THAT THEY WILL BE ABLE TO CATCH UP.

INSIDER: /WE ARE GOING TO GET A SITUATION WHERE WE ARE NEVER GOING TO BE ABLE TO CATCH UP TO OLDER CASES AND THEY WILL BE STRUCK OFF THE ROLL // AND THERE’S VICTIMS THAT. IT WILL NEVER SEE JUSTICE. M9

DEREK: WHAT IF NOTHING DONE?
VANESSA: // WE WOULD BE GOING BACKWARDS ON SUCH GOOD WORK THAT'S BEING DONE. AND I DON'T UNDERSTAND HOW WE CAN ALLOW ONE OF THE GREATEST WEAPONS AVAILABLE TO US TODAY TO BECOME OBSOLETE. IT'S SIMPLY UNIMAGINABLE THAT WOULD BE ALLOWED TO HAPPEN. M20

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Forensic Testing Serivce with the South African Police Serivce have grinded to a halt - we ask why and who should be held accountable.
metadata.Summary: DNA Analysis is the greatest weapon we have against violent crimes ranging from GBV to rape, murder and armed robberies. While we have access to the technology, the expertise and the experience. South Africa is facing a human rights crisis with unprecedented backlogs of forensic exhibits that have not been processed.
metadata.Further information: There has been a 300% increase in the backlog of cases, +/- 90% of which are sexual assault cases. In November 2020 there was a backlog of close to 117736 cases just in the Western Cape, Eastern Cape, KZN and at the SAPS Headquarters. It is estimated to just over 90% of all outstanding analysis are sexual assault kits. In March it was revealed in Parliament that figure has increased to 172000 cases. Not a single sample was processed in all of January and February this year. NOT ONE. Former deputy chair of the National Forensic Oversight and Ethics Board, Vanessa Lynch and director of the DNA Project is outraged. This is a travesty of justice. South Africa is seen as the Jewel in the Crown of DNA analysis on the African Continent – but the country is quickly losing that status despite the infrastructure and skills In 2020 concerns were raised about contract management, especially in light of the admission of lax contract management systems within the division. The Forensic Sciences Laboratory said it need funds – treasury allocated an additional R250 million to the division’s operational baseline budget in November 2020 hoping it would improve functionality. Fast forward 3 months and only 30% of this budget has been spent. Of the 5 contracts that have been waiting to be finalized for the last two years – only two have been finalized – three are still in limbo. The Head of SAPS forensic science labs Maj-Gen Edward Ngokha said his department faced insufficient funding and experienced instability at management level this week when the new appointed Forensic Oversight and Ethics Board appeared before the portfolio committee on Police this week. HOW DO WE TELL THE STORY PAINT A PICTURE OF WHAT DNA ANALYSIS CAN DO Sikhangele Mki was arrested for general assault. His DNA-sample was run against the DNA Porject database. He was linked to multiple violent crimes. He was convicted on 30 counts of rape, 20 counts of kidnapping, four counts of assault with intent to do grievous bodily harm, 12 counts of robbery with aggravating circumstances, six counts of attempted robbery with aggravating circumstances, two counts of robbery and three counts of attempted robbery. He was convicted in the Western Cape High Court in 2017 and is now serving 15 life terms and 120 years imprisonment. He was only caught and convicted after his DNA sample was run through South Africa’s DNA system. THIS ISN’T HAPPENING. VIOLENT CRIMINALS ROAM FREE EVERY DAY PERPATRATING THESE CRIMES WITH IMPUNITY, BECAUSE EVEN IF THEY ARE CAUGHT THEY ARE NOT GOING TO BE CONVICTED ANY TIME SOON. Ironically South Africa was recognized internationally for this case – as a global success case. WHAT DOES THIS FAILURE OF JUSTICE DO TO VICTIMS OF VIOLENT CRIMES Bring in MBali – we paint her not as a victim – but as a survivor. She lives has survived a sexual assault, but lives the secondary trauma every day because the DNA in her case from 14 months ago is not being processed. What she wants is what government has enacted but not enforced. DNA samples should be processed within 30 days, Lynch explains “there is no question that DNA profiling is one of the most successful prosecutorial tools to identify rapists and violent criminals, due to its high rate of reliability in securing conviction. In short, justice delayed is justice denied”. WHO NEEDS TO ANSWER SAPS & THE ETHICS BOARD 1. SAPS allowed this situation to progress to this stage 2. The board does not have an enforceable plan of action. No one is being held liable If we do not hold the authorities accountable how can we hold criminals accountable. Their inaction is criminal. INTERVIEWS 1. Vanessa Lynch – DNA PROJECT – the value of DNA and the current status quo 2. Mbali – survivor or rape 3. SAPS – Head of Forensic Services Laboratories or maybe Brigadier Vish Naidoo 4. Insider – frustrated with processes – criminals caught but not brought to book 5. National Forensic Oversight & Ethics Board
